sources.note: Holds one completed reasoning run fixed and varies only what a monitor is allowed to inspect — response, self-summary, full trace, internals — and finds the summary's value nearly vanishes once the monitor already has the prompt, so monitorability is a property of the display and the reader jointly rather than of the text.
sources.title: How Much Does a Reasoning Summary Reveal? An Observability Ladder for Large Language Models

sources.note: Tags every sentence of a reasoning trace by its function and studies the sequence rather than the content, finding that failing SAT traces collapse into repetitive verification and commit early, that failing UNSAT traces run the wrong procedure entirely, and that a prompt naming the missing procedure recovers 84.6% of them.
sources.title: The Tell-Tale Trace: Detecting Reasoning Failures in LLMs Using Chain-of-Thought Dynamics

sources.note: Decomposes measured self-correction gains into a content margin and format-recovery margins, and shows causally that most of what the field has reported as self-correction is answer-parseability repair.
sources.title: The Calibration Floor: Format Repair Can Masquerade as Self-Correction at Small-to-Mid Scale

sources.note: Spends test-time compute on iteratively refining each sampled rollout rather than on drawing more of them, then majority-votes the refined answers, with no verifier.
sources.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Separates hallucination into a reasoning failure and a knowledge failure, treats the first with a structured reflect-before-answering format and the second with a reward for abstaining when no sampled chain succeeds, and shows the two mechanisms are not interchangeable -- reflection alone never abstains, abstention alone never lowers the hallucination proxy.
sources.title: REIN: Bridging the Gap between Reasoning and Reliability via Reflection and Abstention Alignment

sources.note: Builds a dense process reward without a learned verifier or an online judge, by aligning generated reasoning steps to the process-labelled reference steps that existing datasets already contain using numerical, symbolic and lexical matching rules, gated so a partial reference match cannot override a wrong final answer.
sources.title: StructReward: Efficient Structured Process Rewards for Self-Correcting Multimodal Reasoning

sources.note: Trains self-correction as a step-level preference problem -- preferring a detect-and-repair continuation over the continuation that would follow if the error went unaddressed -- after first initialising with ordinary step-level preference optimisation, and finds that correcting more often and detecting more errors both anti-correlate with accuracy.
sources.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs

sources.note: Profiles the dominant failure mode of an agent task family on development data, then freezes a policy that permits only the recovery interventions matched to that failure -- so a failure decides which repair is admissible and how much evidence to spend, rather than triggering more context indiscriminately.
sources.title: Diagnosis Before Recovery: Turning Agent Failures into Selective Self-Correction

sources.note: Gives a search agent an explicitly reversible trajectory tree with reflect and backtrack as first-class actions, and trains the reflection policy with a dense local signal distilled from a teacher that can see the whole trajectory alongside the sparse terminal reward the local decision is ultimately judged by.
sources.title: LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation

sources.note: Identifies double-checking after the correct answer is already derived as 'invalid thinking', and trains a GRPO variant with a compress reward that targets exactly that portion.
sources.title: Optimizing Length Compression in Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Decomposes mathematical problem-solving into four cognitive dimensions after Polya and tests each separately, finding wide capability gaps that final-answer accuracy hides.
sources.title: SMART: Evaluating LLMs' Mathematical Reasoning via a Human Cognitive Process-Inspired Benchmark

sources.note: Uses 200 mathematical proof problems as a diagnostic, finding some reasoning models solve under 20% and cataloguing 10 fine-grained error types that numerical benchmarks hide.
sources.title: Mathematical Proof as a Litmus Test: Revealing Failure Modes of Advanced Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Routes each generation step among a fast path, a perception re-examination path and a self-reflection path, trained on 790k samples of teacher-attributed perception-versus-reasoning failures.
sources.title: Addressing Overthinking in Large Vision-Language Models via Gated Perception-Reasoning Optimization

sources.note: Adds a Self-Reflection token that lets reasoning models recover from harmful output mid-generation, cutting harmful completion rate from 13.8% to 4.1%.
sources.title: Self-Reflection Improves Safety of Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Turns each intermediate step of a reasoning trajectory into a numerical feature vector of distances to the answer choices, projects those into 2D to visualize how trajectories move through answer space, and reuses the same features to build a lightweight verifier for weighted voting.
sources.title: Landscape of Thoughts: Visualizing the Reasoning Process of Large Language Models

sources.note: Tracks mutual information between each reasoning step's representation and the correct answer, finds it spikes at sparse 'MI peaks' that decode to reflective tokens like 'Wait' and 'Hmm', and shows suppressing exactly those tokens degrades reasoning while suppressing equally many others does not.
sources.title: Demystifying Reasoning Dynamics with Mutual Information: Thinking Tokens are Information Peaks in LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Turns a linear chain of thought into a dependency DAG, labels each node as advancing the frontier or reviewing it, and prunes review nodes on two graph criteria — too few descendants, or too late in the trace — cutting 42% of tokens while accuracy holds or rises.
sources.title: Graph-Based Chain-of-Thought Pruning for Reducing Redundant Reflections in Reasoning LLMs

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:

aliases: string - other names the sources use for the same thing
output_schema.definition: string - two to four sentences defining the entity as the cited sources use it, not as a textbook would
output_schema.kind: string - one of: concept, method, dataset, model
related: string - name of a neighbouring entity worth linking to. Kept as you give it and never derived away, so name what a reader should turn to next rather than what happens to appear alongside this. Answering again replaces the whole list; an empty list retracts

result.definition: A model detecting and repairing its own error, and across 17 sources a capability the archive can measure the behaviour of more easily than the benefit. The central finding is a dissociation: how often a model announces a correction is anti-correlated with whether the corrections help. Against two prior supervised methods on a shared backbone, a step-level preference method scores higher on both mathematics benchmarks while self-correcting at 28.8 and 23.9 percent against 45.3 and 46.5 and recalling fewer errors, and two of its own five backbones lower their correction rate after training while improving. The diagnosis offered is behaviour collapse under supervised training, which biases a model toward following correction templates rather than selectively revising real errors. Two measurement problems follow. The behavioural metrics are defined by matching a list of signal phrases, so a model that corrects without using one is invisible to the measurement, and the training data's preferred continuations are defined by the same convention. And the construct has almost no clean measurement window: models weak enough to have headroom lack the signal, models with the signal lack the headroom, so the design space where self-correction could be measured cleanly is nearly empty -- one source's calibration-floor argument finds only one marginally viable cell with negligible held-out gain. Where the archive finds it working is as a trained selectivity rather than a prompted behaviour, with the preference formed between a repair and the continuation that would have followed had the error stood, so the signal exists only where an error does.
